package_info.package_name: NSIS-based packer (various malware families: XLoader, AgentTesla, Remcos, etc.)
package_info.package_versions: Multiple unique hashes (see IOCs); not versioned in the traditional sense
package_info.why_malicious: The NSIS-based packages are used exclusively as malware droppers, embedding encrypted payloads and custom DLLs or executables that decrypt and execute additional malware (such as AgentTesla, Remcos, XLoader, etc.). The entire package is malicious because its only function is to deliver, decrypt, and execute further malware on the victim's system, with no legitimate installation purpose.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, immediately after the NSIS installer is executed and unpacks files
required_permissions: filesystem (to read and write files in $PLUGINSDIR)
process injection (to execute shellcode or inject into other processes)
network (by payload, for C2 or exfiltration)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Pseudocode representing DLL loader logic
Load encrypted payload from NSIS archive
Extract decryption key from DLL resource or hardcoded value
Decrypt payload using custom algorithm (e.g., RC4)
Allocate memory for shellcode
Copy decrypted shellcode to memory
Execute shellcode (e.g., via CreateThread or process injection)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the NSIS installer unpacks files, the malicious DLL loads an encrypted payload from the NSIS archive, extracts a decryption key from a resource or hardcoded value, decrypts the payload using a custom algorithm, allocates memory for the shellcode, copies the decrypted shellcode into memory, and executes it (typically via CreateThread or process injection), resulting in the launch of the actual malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLLs in $PLUGINSDIR are not expected to decrypt and execute arbitrary code. The presence of custom decryption logic, memory allocation for shellcode, and direct execution of decrypted code are hallmarks of malware droppers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal NSIS plugins are designed to provide installation features, not to decrypt and execute hidden payloads or perform process injection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software installers may use plugins for custom install logic, but do not decrypt and execute hidden code or perform process injection.
key_indicators: Custom decryption routines present in DLL code
Memory allocation and direct shellcode execution
Encrypted payloads bundled within the installer
DLLs in $PLUGINSDIR with no legitimate plugin functionality

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, immediately after the DLL or EXE decrypts and loads the shellcode into memory
required_permissions: Windows API access (to resolve and call system functions)
network (by payload, for C2 communication and exfiltration)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Pseudocode for shellcode
Resolve Windows API functions by hash
Establish C2 communication
Download or execute further payloads
Exfiltrate data or perform keylogging
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the DLL or EXE decrypts and loads the shellcode, the shellcode resolves Windows API functions by hash, establishes command-and-control (C2) communication, downloads or executes additional payloads, and may exfiltrate data or perform keylogging, resulting in active malicious operations on the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Shellcode that dynamically resolves Windows APIs by hash and initiates C2 communication is a classic malware technique to evade static detection and perform malicious actions such as data theft or further payload delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not contain or execute shellcode that performs API resolution by hash, establishes C2 channels, or exfiltrates data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing frameworks and red team tools may use similar techniques for authorized testing, but not in production installers.
key_indicators: API resolution by hash within shellcode
C2 communication routines embedded in shellcode
Behavioral patterns matching known malware families (e.g., AgentTesla, Remcos, XLoader)

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the NSIS installer executes a malicious EXE variant instead of a DLL
required_permissions: filesystem (to read resources and write to disk)
process creation (to launch or inject into other processes)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Pseudocode for EXE variant
Read encrypted payload from resource
Decrypt payload using embedded key
Inject payload into new or existing process
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the NSIS installer executes the malicious EXE, the executable reads an encrypted payload from its resources, decrypts it using an embedded key, and injects the decrypted payload into a new or existing process, enabling stealthy execution of the malware without dropping files to disk.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process injection and resource-based payload decryption are advanced malware techniques designed to evade detection and are not found in legitimate installers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal installer executables do not perform process injection or decrypt and execute hidden payloads from resources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software updaters may use self-extracting archives, but do not perform process injection or hidden payload decryption.
key_indicators: Encrypted payloads stored as resources in EXE
Process injection logic present in executable

attack_chain.action: User executes the NSIS installer, which unpacks files to a temporary directory ($PLUGINSDIR).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious DLL or EXE is loaded and executed from $PLUGINSDIR.

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL or EXE loads and decrypts the embedded/encrypted payload using a custom algorithm and key.
attack_chain.leads_to: Decrypted shellcode is prepared and loaded into process memory.

attack_chain.action: Decrypted shellcode is executed in memory, resolving Windows APIs by hash and establishing C2 communication.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware payload (AgentTesla, Remcos, XLoader, etc.) is launched and begins malicious activity such as data exfiltration, keylogging, or further payload delivery.

behavioral_signatures: NSIS installer drops DLL or EXE to $PLUGINSDIR and immediately loads or executes it
DLL/EXE performs decryption of embedded or encrypted payload using custom algorithms
In-memory execution of shellcode that resolves Windows APIs by hash
Process injection or memory allocation for shellcode execution
Absence of legitimate installation actions in plugin or EXE
file_indicators: Presence of suspicious DLLs or EXEs in $PLUGINSDIR during or immediately after install
Encrypted blobs or resources within installer or plugin files (e.g., large binary resources in DLL/EXE)
Unusual or obfuscated plugin or executable names in $PLUGINSDIR
Installer files with no legitimate installation logic
network_indicators: C2 communication initiated by payload (domains, IPs, or protocols vary by malware family)
Unusual outbound connections from the installer process or its child processes immediately after execution
Network activity to known malicious infrastructure associated with AgentTesla, Remcos, XLoader, etc.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor NSIS installer execution for the creation and loading of DLLs or EXEs in $PLUGINSDIR, especially those that allocate memory and execute code in-process. Analyze plugins and executables for custom decryption routines, resource-based encrypted payloads, and shellcode execution. Use memory analysis to detect in-memory shellcode and API resolution by hash. Correlate with known IOCs (hashes, domains, IPs) and monitor for suspicious outbound network activity following installer execution. Flag installers that lack legitimate installation logic or whose plugins/executables perform process injection or in-memory code execution.
